quote: The Bill of Sale definition omits the "other than the Excluded Assets" language. The Excluded Assets (APA § 2.2) are Seller's cash, the Albany manufacturing facility, and the HOLLIS trademark. As drafted, the Bill of Sale could be read to convey all three to Buyer. ... The Bill of Sale is the operative conveyance document. If its definition of "Purchased Assets" controls over the APA's (see Issue 7 below regarding the order-of-precedence provision) ... Recommended Fix. Amend Bill of Sale § 1.1(b) to track the APA definition exactly ... other than the Excluded Assets ... For the avoidance of doubt, the Excluded Assets (as defined in Section 2.2 of the Purchase Agreement) are not Purchased Assets and are not conveyed by this Bill of Sale.
reason: The memo's Issue 2 meets every element of the criterion. It names the Bill of Sale's 'Purchased Assets' definition, which covers all assets used or held for use in the Business and has no Excluded-Assets carve-out. It lists the retained assets that could be conveyed (cash, the Albany facility, HOLLIS). It explains that the Bill of Sale is the conveyance instrument and may control under APA § 10.12. It recommends tracking the APA definition and expressly excluding the Excluded Assets. One weakness: the memo treats § 10.12 control as uncertain ('If its definition ... controls') rather than stating it, but Issue 7 says the subject-matter clause would let the Bill of Sale control, so the substance is there.
